positive.prompt: Here's a raw user story: 'As a user, I want to export my invoices as CSV.' Run this end to end and ship it.
Bug report: checkout hangs intermittently after the last release. Drive this to a fix autonomously, I don't want to name which agent handles what.
Take this feature request and run the whole team on it without me picking personas or commands.

negative.prompt: Review this PR for correctness and security issues.
Write unit tests for the checkout discount calculator.

evals.prompt: Raw user story: 'As a shopper, I want to save items to a wishlist.' No persona or command named — drive this autonomously end to end.
evals.expected_output: Classification as New Feature/User Story, a staged plan (requirements/product -> architecture -> build -> review -> QA -> ship), a workflow-state.json initialized and updated per stage, and a final report listing which gates passed with evidence pointers.
expectations: Request is classified before any implementation work starts
A stage plan is produced naming which persona owns each stage
Workflow state is recorded/updated at each stage transition, not just summarized at the end
Review and QA both sign off before a deployment-agent stage is reached
If review or QA reject the work, the loop routes back to the originating developer persona with a structured report rather than the orchestrator fixing it directly
